newsitem.title: USA: InterCel to offer $300 mln senior notes.
newsitem.headline: InterCel to offer $300 mln senior notes.

text.p: Personal communications company InterCel Inc said Monday it planned to issue $300 million in senior notes due 2007 to buy licenses for basic trading areas in two U.S. states.

InterCel, which provides personal communications services or PCS under the brand name Powertel, also said it had closed into escrow the sale of 50,000 shares of Series C convertible preferred stock for $22.5 million in cash to The Huff Alternative Income Fund LP. It said it did the same with 50,000 shares of Series D convertible preferred stock for $22.5 million in cash to SCANA Communications Inc.
The funds will be released from escrow upon the closing of the sale of the senior notes by April 30, InterCel said.
The convertible stocks become convertible into InterCel common stock at a conversion ratio equal to $12.75 per share of common stock, it said.

InterCel said it would use the proceeds from the sale of the convertible stocks and the notes to buy licenses for 13 Basic Trading Areas in Kentucky and Tennessee, to finance development, construction and operating costs associated with its PCS system.
It said it would also use some of the money to finance the first six interest payments on the notes.
